questions.questionText: Milk and water are in the ratio 7:5 in a 144 litre mixture. Find the quantity of milk.
questions.solution: Total parts = 12. One part = 144/12 = 12. Milk = 7×12 = 84 litres.

questions.questionText: Milk and water are in the ratio 5:4 in an 81 litre mixture. Find the quantity of water.
questions.solution: Total parts = 9. One part = 81/9 = 9. Water = 4×9 = 36 litres.

questions.questionText: Milk and water are in the ratio 3:2 in a 60 litre mixture. How much water should be added to make the ratio 3:5?
questions.solution: Milk = 36 litres, water = 24 litres. Milk stays fixed. In new ratio 3:5, 3 parts = 36, so 1 part = 12. Required water = 5×12 = 60. Water added = 60−24 = 36 litres.

questions.questionText: Milk and water are in the ratio 9:4 in a 104 litre mixture. How much milk should be added to make the ratio 11:4?
questions.solution: Total parts = 13, so 1 part = 8. Milk = 72, water = 32. Water stays fixed. In new ratio 11:4, 4 parts = 32, so 1 part = 8. Required milk = 88. Milk added = 88−72 = 16 litres.

questions.questionText: A 75 litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4:1. If 15 litres of mixture is removed, find the quantity of milk left.
questions.solution: After removing mixture, ratio remains 4:1. Remaining mixture = 60 litres. Milk = 4/5 × 60 = 48 litres.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 90 litres of pure milk. 30 litres is removed and replaced with water once. Find the quantity of milk left.
questions.solution: Survival factor = (90−30)/90 = 2/3. Milk left = 90×2/3 = 60 litres.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 100 litres of pure milk. 20 litres is removed and replaced with water twice. Find the quantity of milk left.
questions.solution: Survival factor each time = 80/100 = 4/5. Milk left = 100×4/5×4/5 = 64 litres.

questions.questionText: A vessel contains 72 litres of pure milk. 18 litres is removed and replaced with water twice. Find the quantity of milk left.
questions.solution: Survival factor = 54/72 = 3/4. Milk left = 72×3/4×3/4 = 40.5 litres.

questions.questionText: An 80 litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3:1. 20 litres of the mixture is removed and replaced with water. Find the new ratio of milk to water.
questions.solution: Initial milk = 60, water = 20. Removed 20 litres in 3:1 ratio, so removed milk = 15 and water = 5. Left milk = 45, water = 15. Add 20 litres water, new water = 35. Ratio = 45:35 = 9:7.

questions.questionText: A 90 litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7:2. If 18 litres of mixture is removed and replaced with water, find the quantity of milk left.
questions.solution: Initial milk = 70 litres. Survival factor = (90−18)/90 = 4/5. Milk left = 70×4/5 = 56 litres.

questions.questionText: A vessel has 100 litres of mixture of milk and water in the ratio 4:1. 25 litres of mixture is removed and replaced with water twice. Find the quantity of milk left after two operations.
questions.solution: Initial milk = 80 litres. Survival factor each time = 75/100 = 3/4. Milk left = 80×3/4×3/4 = 45 litres.

questions.questionText: A 120 litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 5:3. If 24 litres of mixture is removed and replaced with water twice, find the quantity of milk left.
questions.solution: Initial milk = 75 litres. Survival factor each time = 96/120 = 4/5. Milk left = 75×4/5×4/5 = 48 litres.

questions.questionText: Tea costing ₹80 per kg is mixed with tea costing ₹120 per kg to get a mixture costing ₹95 per kg. Find the ratio of cheaper tea to dearer tea.
questions.solution: By alligation, cheaper:dearer = (120−95):(95−80) = 25:15 = 5:3.

questions.questionText: Tea costing ₹90 per kg is mixed with tea costing ₹150 per kg to get a mixture costing ₹110 per kg. Find the ratio of cheaper tea to dearer tea.
questions.solution: By alligation, cheaper:dearer = (150−110):(110−90) = 40:20 = 2:1.

questions.questionText: A 30% acid solution is mixed with a 70% acid solution to get a 45% acid solution. Find the ratio of 30% solution to 70% solution.
questions.solution: By alligation, 30% solution:70% solution = (70−45):(45−30) = 25:15 = 5:3.

questions.questionText: A 30% acid solution is mixed with a 60% acid solution to get a 45% acid solution. Find the ratio of 30% solution to 60% solution.
questions.solution: By alligation, 30% solution:60% solution = (60−45):(45−30) = 15:15 = 1:1.

questions.questionText: Rice costing ₹42 per kg and ₹56 per kg are mixed in the ratio 3:4. Find the average cost per kg.
20 kg rice at ₹45 per kg is mixed with 30 kg rice at ₹55 per kg. The mixture is sold at ₹60 per kg. Find the total profit.
Sugar costing ₹36 per kg and ₹48 per kg are mixed. The mixture is sold at ₹50 per kg at 25% profit. Find the ratio of cheaper sugar to dearer sugar.
questions.solution: CP of mixture = 50/1.25 = ₹40. By alligation, cheaper:dearer = (48−40):(40−36) = 8:4 = 2:1.

questions.questionText: Two types of pulses costing ₹90 per kg and ₹150 per kg are blended and sold at ₹250 per kg, gaining 25%. Find the ratio of cheaper pulse to dearer pulse.
questions.solution: CP of mixture = 250/1.25 = ₹200? Since ₹200 is above both ₹90 and ₹150, this is impossible. Corrected interpretation: To make valid alligation, selling price should be ₹125 at 25% profit, giving CP mixture ₹100. Then ratio = (150−100):(100−90)=50:10=5:1. This question is invalid.

questions.questionText: A 75 litre solution contains 40% alcohol. How much water should be added to make it 30% alcohol?
questions.solution: Alcohol = 40% of 75 = 30 litres. For 30% solution, total mixture = 30×100/30 = 100 litres. Water added = 100−75 = 25 litres.

questions.questionText: A 60 litre solution contains 40% acid. How much water should be added to make it 25% acid?
questions.solution: Acid = 40% of 60 = 24 litres. For 25% solution, total mixture = 24×100/25 = 96 litres. Water added = 96−60 = 36 litres.

questions.questionText: An 80 litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 5:3. How much water must be added to make the ratio of milk to water 2:3?
questions.solution: Milk = 50 litres, water = 30 litres. Milk stays fixed. In new ratio 2:3, 2 parts = 50, so 1 part = 25. Required water = 75 litres. Water added = 75−30 = 45 litres.

questions.questionText: Milk and water are in the ratio 11:5 in an 80 litre mixture. How much water should be added to make the ratio 11:9?
questions.solution: Total parts = 16, so 1 part = 5. Milk = 55, water = 25. Milk stays fixed. For ratio 11:9, 11 parts = 55, so 1 part = 5. Required water = 45. Water added = 45−25 = 20 litres.

questions.questionText: A 54 litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7:2. How much water should be added to make the ratio 7:5?
questions.solution: Total parts = 9, so 1 part = 6. Milk = 42, water = 12. Milk stays fixed. In new ratio 7:5, 7 parts = 42, so 1 part = 6. Required water = 30. Water added = 30−12 = 18 litres.
